title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Sharia Islam Worship And Supplication

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the Sacred Law brought by the Prophet in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as unmatched in its kind and excellence, with no equal in existence or possibility.

questions.question: How does the passage show the long-term impact of that Law on human life?
questions.answer: It says that for fourteen centuries it has guided and governed a large part of humanity with justice and precision.

questions.question: What detail shows the scale of the Law’s influence?
questions.answer: It is described as administering the lives of one fifth of humanity.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the source from which Islam emerged?
questions.answer: It came forth from the Prophet’s actions, words, and inner spiritual condition.

questions.question: In what ways is Islam described as benefiting believers in every century?
questions.answer: It guides and shelters them, teaches their minds, lights and cleanses their hearts, trains their souls, and helps their spirits grow.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by repeating that nothing like this religion exists or could exist?
questions.answer: It emphasizes its uniqueness and perfection beyond any rival.

questions.question: How is the Prophet’s worship described in comparison with others?
questions.answer: He is shown as the leading example in practicing all forms of worship in his religion.

questions.question: What qualities are especially mentioned in his worship?
questions.answer: Deep piety, fear of Allah, full performance of worship, and careful attention to its deepest meanings.

questions.question: What makes his worship especially remarkable during difficult times?
questions.answer: He kept up complete and profound worship even while living with constant struggle and activity.

questions.question: What is the Jawshan al-Kabir used to show in this passage?
questions.answer: It is used to show the extraordinary depth of his knowledge of Allah in prayer.

questions.question: How does the passage compare later saints and knowers of Allah with the Prophet in describing Allah?
questions.answer: It says that even together they could not reach his level of knowledge and accurate description.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about him in the area of supplication?
questions.answer: It concludes that he has no equal in prayer as well.

questions.question: Why is the beginning of the Treatise On Supplicatory Prayer mentioned?
questions.answer: It is given as a place where a reader can see part of the meaning and greatness of the Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What overall picture of the Prophet does this passage build?
questions.answer: It presents him as unique in law, religion, worship, spiritual knowledge, and prayer.

questions.question: Why is the Sacred Law described as having no equal?
questions.answer: Because it has ruled justly and accurately over a huge portion of humanity for many centuries.

questions.question: What two qualities are joined together in the passage’s description of that Law’s rule?
questions.answer: Justice and precision.

questions.question: According to the passage, how is Islam connected to the Prophet personally?
questions.answer: It is shown as flowing from his life, speech, and inner state.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam does for people’s intellects?
questions.answer: It teaches and educates them.

questions.question: What does it say Islam does for people’s hearts and souls?
questions.answer: It enlightens and purifies the heart and refines and disciplines the soul.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam does for the human spirit?
questions.answer: It becomes a means for its growth and advancement.

questions.question: How is the Prophet’s place in worship ranked among his followers?
questions.answer: He is described as the first and foremost in practicing it.

questions.question: Which inner attitude toward Allah is highlighted in his worship?
questions.answer: Strong piety and reverent fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the completeness of his worship?
questions.answer: He fulfilled its duties fully and paid attention to its deepest dimensions.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Jawshan al-Kabir to knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: It says that through it he described his Lord with a level of insight unmatched by later spiritual masters.

questions.question: What inference can be made from the statement that later saints could not reach his level even together?
questions.answer: His spiritual understanding was exceptionally high and beyond ordinary human comparison.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning one of the ninety-nine sections of the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: To point readers to an example that displays its richness and uniqueness.

questions.question: What final judgment does the passage make about the Jawshan al-Kabir itself?
questions.answer: It says that it too stands without an equal.

questions.question: What subjects are used in this passage to demonstrate the Prophet’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: His Sacred Law, Islam, worship, supplications, and knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: What time span is used to support the greatness of the Law he brought?
questions.answer: Fourteen centuries.

questions.question: How does the passage measure the human reach of that Law?
questions.answer: By saying it has administered the lives of one fifth of humanity.

questions.question: What effects of Islam on human development are listed in the passage?
questions.answer: It guides the mind, purifies the heart, disciplines the soul, and advances the spirit.

questions.question: What does the word “refuge” suggest about Islam’s role for believers?
questions.answer: It gives them protection, stability, and a place of safety in life.

questions.question: What made the Prophet’s worship stand out besides being first in practice?
questions.answer: He lived it with the highest piety and with full awareness of its deepest meanings.

questions.question: How does the passage connect worship with struggle?
questions.answer: It shows that he maintained perfect worship even while facing ongoing effort and hardship.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the beginning and end of worship suggest?
questions.answer: His servitude to Allah was complete from start to finish.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the Jawshan al-Kabir mainly demonstrate?
questions.answer: It demonstrates his unmatched insight into and description of his Sustainer.

questions.question: Who are said to be unable to equal his degree of gnosis?
questions.answer: All the saints and knowers of Allah who came after him, even working together.

questions.question: What kind of evidence is the reader invited to examine personally?
questions.answer: A section from the beginning of the Treatise On Supplicatory Prayer that explains part of the Jawshan’s meaning.

questions.question: Based on the passage, what relationship exists between prayer and knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: His prayers show very deep recognition and understanding of Allah.

questions.question: What conclusion about the Prophet can be drawn from all these descriptions together?
questions.answer: He is presented as the unsurpassed model of religion in both outward practice and inward spirituality.

questions.question: What is said about the possibility of producing a religion or law equal to what the Prophet brought?
questions.answer: The passage says neither an equal nor something more perfect exists or could exist.

questions.question: What reason is given for the excellence of the Sacred Law?
questions.answer: It has governed a vast portion of humanity for centuries in a fair and careful way.

questions.question: From what three parts of the Prophet’s life is Islam said to have emerged?
questions.answer: From his deeds, his speech, and his inward condition.

questions.question: How is Islam portrayed in relation to reason?
questions.answer: It is a teacher and trainer for the intellect.

questions.question: How is Islam portrayed in relation to the heart?
questions.answer: It gives light to the heart and cleanses it.

questions.question: How is Islam portrayed in relation to the soul and spirit?
questions.answer: It disciplines the soul and helps the spirit move forward and develop.

questions.question: What makes the Prophet the best example in worship according to the passage?
questions.answer: He practiced every form of worship first and most fully, with the greatest piety.

questions.question: Why is it important that he worshipped while engaged in constant activity?
questions.answer: It shows his devotion was steady and sincere, not dependent on an easy life.

questions.question: Which prayer collection is singled out as especially important here?
questions.answer: The Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does the passage say this prayer collection reveals about him?
questions.answer: It reveals an unmatched level of spiritual knowledge and precise praise of Allah.

questions.question: How are later gnostics and saints used as a comparison point?
questions.answer: Their combined efforts are said to fall short of his level, which highlights his superiority.

questions.question: What would a thoughtful reader conclude after studying the mentioned explanation of the Jawshan?
questions.answer: That the Jawshan al-Kabir itself is also without a peer.

questions.question: What repeated idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The repeated idea is that the Prophet has no equal in the matters being discussed.

questions.question: In what practical area of life is the Sacred Law said to have shown its excellence?
questions.answer: In ruling and organizing human life over a large community across many centuries.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the fairness of that rule?
questions.answer: It describes it as just and exact.

questions.question: According to the passage, how widely has Islam served people over time?
questions.answer: In every century it has served hundreds of millions of people.

questions.question: What roles does Islam fill for those people?
questions.answer: It acts as a guide, a shelter, a teacher, a purifier, a trainer, and a source of spiritual growth.

questions.question: What part of the Prophet’s example proves his excellence in worship?
questions.answer: He performed all forms of worship first, best, and with the deepest awareness.

questions.question: Which two inner qualities are directly connected to his worship?
questions.answer: God-consciousness and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage indicate about the consistency of his devotion?
questions.answer: It remained complete even during a life full of effort and action.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the quality of his prayers?
questions.answer: They are presented as extremely rich in knowledge of Allah and unmatched in depth.

questions.question: What does the word “gnosis” point to in this passage?
questions.answer: A deep spiritual knowing and recognition of Allah.

questions.question: Why is the comparison with later saints important?
questions.answer: It strengthens the claim that his understanding of Allah was greater than theirs.

questions.question: What text is recommended for seeing part of the meaning of the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: The opening section of the Treatise On Supplicatory Prayer.

questions.question: If someone asked for one proof from this passage that the Prophet was unmatched inwardly as well as outwardly, what could be given?
questions.answer: His worship was outwardly perfect, and his prayers showed an inward knowledge of Allah beyond all later saints.

questions.question: What balance between outer religion and inner faith does this passage present?
questions.answer: It presents both strong law and deep spirituality together in a complete way.

questions.question: What central message about the Prophet is supported by all parts of this passage?
questions.answer: He is portrayed as uniquely perfect in what he brought and in how he lived it.

questions.question: How does the passage argue for the uniqueness of the Sacred Law?
questions.answer: By pointing to its unmatched justice, precision, duration, and influence over a major share of humanity.

questions.question: What does the phrase about one fifth of humanity help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see the vast reach and historical strength of that Law.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying Islam came from the Prophet’s deeds, sayings, and inward states?
questions.answer: It shows that the religion was fully embodied in his whole life, outwardly and inwardly.

questions.question: Name two ways the passage says Islam helps a believer’s inner life.
questions.answer: It purifies the heart and trains the soul.

questions.question: Name two ways the passage says Islam helps a believer’s mind and spirit.
questions.answer: It educates the intellect and advances the spirit.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Prophet as a model of worship?
questions.answer: It presents him as the earliest, most complete, and most reverent practitioner of all its forms.

questions.question: What makes his worship more impressive than ordinary devotion?
questions.answer: He maintained full and deep worship while carrying heavy responsibilities and struggles.

questions.question: What special role does the Jawshan al-Kabir play in the argument of this passage?
questions.answer: It serves as evidence of his unmatched prayer and profound knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: How is his description of Allah evaluated in comparison to later spiritual figures?
questions.answer: It is judged higher and more accurate than what they could reach even together.

questions.question: What skill of the Prophet is especially highlighted through the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: His ability to know, praise, and describe his Sustainer in an extraordinary way.

questions.question: What is the effect of referring readers to another treatise that explains part of the Jawshan?
questions.answer: It invites them to verify for themselves the greatness being claimed.

questions.question: What conclusion about religion and character can be inferred from the whole passage?
questions.answer: The one who brought this religion is shown as unmatched in both teaching and personal devotion.
